quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What is the amount of alcohol in the blood called?

options.text: Implied consent (IC).
Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).

questions.correctAnswerText: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in your blood. A higher BAC means you are more impaired.

questions.question: When weather or light makes it hard to see while driving, which lights should you use?

options.text: Use your parking lights.
Use your high beams.
Use your low beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, snow, or rain. High beams reflect off these conditions and create glare, making it harder to see.

questions.question: What must you do when a school bus is picking up or dropping off children?

options.text: Stop, regardless of your direction of travel.
Stop if you are driving in the same direction.
Slow down and be prepared to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, regardless of your direction of travel.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop before reaching a school bus that is picking up or dropping off children. This applies no matter which direction you are traveling.

questions.question: When should you allow extra space between your vehicle and the car ahead?

options.text: When following a station wagon.
When following a driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle.
When following a small passenger car.

questions.correctAnswerText: When following a driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Drivers of trucks, buses, vans, and vehicles pulling trailers cannot see directly behind them. Increase your following distance so they can see you. Large vehicles also block your view ahead, so stay farther back.

questions.question: What does this orange triangle symbol mean?

options.text: Dangerous intersections.
Slow-moving vehicles.
Yield signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicles.
questions.explanation: A reflective orange triangle on the rear of a vehicle warns that it travels slowly. You may see this on farm equipment, roadwork vehicles, or horse-drawn wagons. At night, it appears as a hollow red triangle.

questions.question: When must you always stop before crossing railroad tracks?

options.text: There isn't room on the other side for you to completely cross the tracks.
The railroad crossing is located in a city or town that has frequent train traffic.
You are transporting two or more young children in a passenger vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: There isn't room on the other side for you to completely cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: A train can come at any time on any track. Make sure your vehicle completely clears the tracks before you stop. Never stop while on the tracks.

questions.question: What safe following distance should you maintain when driving near a distracted driver?

options.text: One to two seconds.
Two to three seconds.
Three to four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Three to four seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep three to four seconds of distance between you and a distracted driver. Be extra careful when passing them because they may not see you and could drift into your path.

questions.question: Which lane should you be in before turning left from a one-way street?

options.text: The lane nearest the left curb.
The lane nearest the center of the street.
The lane nearest the right curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane nearest the left curb.
questions.explanation: Always turn from the lane closest to the direction you want to go. For a left turn from a one-way street, use the lane nearest to the left curb.

questions.question: How can you prevent yourself from becoming an aggressive driver?

options.text: Relax and concentrate on driving.
Drive above the posted speed limit.
Tailgate the driver in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax and concentrate on driving.
questions.explanation: Focus on your driving and don't take other drivers' actions personally. Plan enough travel time, follow speed limits, and forgive other drivers' mistakes.

questions.question: You hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the parked vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the parked vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked vehicle or property, you must leave a note with your name, phone number, and address attached to the vehicle or property you hit.

questions.question: A 16- or 17-year-old driver convicted of using an electronic device while driving may face:

options.text: A $500 fine.
A 10-day license suspension.
A 30-day license suspension.

questions.correctAnswerText: A 30-day license suspension.
questions.explanation: Drivers under 18 cannot use a cell phone or electronic device while driving, even hands-free. If convicted, they must take a driver retraining course. Any additional moving violation within three years after completing the course will result in at least a 30-day license suspension.

questions.question: When parking next to a curb, you should use your turn signal:

options.text: Only when pulling away from the curb.
When pulling next to the curb, but not when pulling away.
When pulling next to the curb and when pulling away from it.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pulling next to the curb and when pulling away from it.
questions.explanation: You should signal both when pulling up to a curb and when pulling away from it.

questions.question: Your hands should be placed on the steering wheel at:

options.text: 9 and 3 o'clock.
11 and 4 o'clock.
9 and 12 o'clock.

questions.correctAnswerText: 9 and 3 o'clock.
questions.explanation: Place your hands on opposite sides of the wheel. Your left hand should be between 8 and 10 o'clock, and your right hand between 2 and 4 o'clock. This position allows you to turn without removing your hands from the wheel, especially on highways.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: All traffic must turn left.
No left turn.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a left turn at this location. It is illegal and unsafe to turn left where this sign is posted.

questions.question: When a school bus has its red lights flashing, you must stay stopped until:

options.text: All students are off the bus.
The stop arm is pulled back in.
The stop arm is pulled back in and the bus starts moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: The stop arm is pulled back in and the bus starts moving.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has red lights flashing and its stop arm extended, you must stay stopped. You can proceed only after the lights turn off, the stop arm is pulled in, and the bus begins moving again.

questions.question: At an intersection with a flashing red traffic signal, you must:

options.text: Stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go.
Slow down and drive carefully.
Stop and stay stopped until the light changes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go.
questions.explanation: Treat a flashing red light like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, make sure the way is clear by checking for traffic and pedestrians, then proceed.

questions.question: When driving behind a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.
Drive more slowly.
Keep a larger distance between your car and the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a larger distance between your car and the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Stay at least three to four seconds behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop very quickly, and following too closely is dangerous for both drivers. If a motorcycle falls, you need extra space to avoid hitting the rider. The risk of falling is highest on wet or icy roads, gravel, and metal surfaces like bridges and railroad tracks.

questions.question: Hydroplaning can happen when water is on the road. Your vehicle may hydroplane at speeds as low as:

options.text: 45 miles per hour.
35 miles per hour.
40 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: 35 miles per hour.
questions.explanation: At speeds up to 35 mph, most tires can move water away from the tire surface. When you go faster than 35 mph, tires cannot move water as well. The tires may lose grip on the road and slide over the water like water skis.

questions.question: You are in a left turn lane at an intersection with oncoming traffic. You should:

options.text: Move to the left side of your lane.
Signal before you reach the intersection.
Turn your front wheels to the left to get ready.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal before you reach the intersection.
questions.explanation: Start signaling about 100 feet before you turn. Keep your front wheels straight until it is safe to turn. This protects you if another vehicle hits you from behind—it will not push you into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: You should not stop suddenly in front of a large truck or bus because:

options.text: Small vehicle drivers cannot see large trucks and buses well in their mirrors.
Large trucks and buses need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles.
Large trucks and buses travel faster than small vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks and buses need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need longer distances to stop and start than smaller vehicles. A sudden stop in front of a large vehicle is dangerous because the driver may not be able to stop in time to avoid hitting you.

questions.question: When backing up, what should you do?

options.text: Look through the rear window.
Press hard on the gas pedal.
Rely only on your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: When backing up, put your right arm on the back of the passenger seat and look directly out the rear window. Do not rely on mirrors because they cannot show what is directly behind your vehicle. Always back up slowly.

questions.question: You are coming to an intersection with a flashing red light. You should:

options.text: Slow down and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Come to a complete stop, check the traffic, and go when it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop, check the traffic, and go when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop completely, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: In rainy weather, when should you be most careful when turning or stopping?

options.text: After it has been raining all day.
One half hour after it stops raining.
During the first half hour of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first half hour of rain.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful during the first half hour of rain. During this time, oil from cars mixes with rain on the road surface, creating a slippery layer.

questions.question: If your vehicle loses traction because of water on the road, you should:

options.text: Drive at a constant speed to gain better traction.
Apply the brakes firmly to prevent your vehicle from sliding.
Slow down gradually and not apply the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and not apply the brakes.
questions.explanation: When driving in heavy rain, your tires can lose contact with the road and ride on a layer of water. This is called hydroplaning. If this happens, slow down gradually and do not use the brakes.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Winding road
Loose gravel
Slippery when wet

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road may be slippery when wet. Drive carefully on slippery roads.
